subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw replace the current single chat/agent run deadline with an activity-aware idle timeout plus a hard max-run cap, and how should that map onto existing `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`?
rationale: The remaining work changes core timeout semantics, resource-safety expectations, and possibly config/default behavior, and the related open PRs do not settle that product contract.

options.title: Define idle plus hard cap
options.body: Choose the idle-vs-hard-cap contract first, then review or request a focused implementation that preserves a bounded safety net and user-visible timeout reporting.

options.title: Land only narrow mitigations
options.body: Review the timeout-notice and subagent-heartbeat PRs separately while keeping this issue open for the broader run-budget contract.

options.title: Keep wall-clock semantics
options.body: Treat the current long default plus explicit timeout overrides as sufficient and narrow the remaining work to timeout messaging only.

recommendation.title: Define idle plus hard cap
recommendation.body: Choose the idle-vs-hard-cap contract first, then review or request a focused implementation that preserves a bounded safety net and user-visible timeout reporting.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest routing candidate from the cross-surface runtime history and prior review context.
